idea_summary: A comprehensive appointment booking platform allowing customers to discover local service providers, view timezone-aware availability, and book appointments, while empowering providers to configure schedules, manage service offerings, and enforce automated cancellation policies with robust concurrency controls to prevent double bookings.

functional_requirements.statement: Providers shall be able to define operating hours, buffer times, and service durations in their local timezone.
acceptance_criteria: Provider sets availability schedules with specific timezone metadata.
System converts and persists working intervals in standard UTC format.
Providers can view their localized agenda.

functional_requirements.statement: Customers shall be able to browse available time slots converted to their local or selected timezone and book an appointment without overlapping existing confirmed bookings.
acceptance_criteria: Time slots are accurately projected in the customer's selected timezone.
Concurrent booking attempts for the same slot result in exactly one successful confirmation and atomic rejection of competing requests.
Double bookings are strictly prevented via transactional database locks.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall enforce role-based access control distinguishing customers, providers, and system administrators.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can only view and manage their own bookings.
Providers can only manage their own schedules, services, and client appointments.
Unauthorized cross-role endpoint access returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.

functional_requirements.statement: The platform shall enforce a configurable cancellation policy allowing appointment cancellation and refund handling according to provider-defined cutoff windows.
acceptance_criteria: Cancellations requested prior to the cutoff threshold are processed automatically with full or partial refunds.
Cancellations attempted after the cutoff window are rejected or flagged for manual provider review.
Freed appointment slots immediately become available for other customers.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The booking transaction engine must maintain strict serializability under high concurrency to prevent duplicate bookings.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero duplicate bookings under 500 concurrent booking requests per provider slot
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated concurrent stress testing using distributed load generators simulating simultaneous slot checkout.

non_functional_requirements.statement: All scheduling calculations and persistence layers must maintain sub-second latency across international timezones.
non_functional_requirements.target: P95 response time under 200ms for availability queries across all timezones
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Performance benchmarking with synthetic data across 50 distinct IANA timezones.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Authentication tokens and sensitive customer PII must be protected in transit and at rest with strict role validation.
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% compliance with OAuth2/JWT role authorization standards and zero unauthenticated data leaks
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Automated static security scanning and dynamic penetration testing suites.

architecture_components.name: Identity and Access Management Service
responsibilities: Issue role-scoped claims for customer and provider personas.

architecture_components.name: Availability and Scheduling Engine
responsibilities: Calculate real-time slot availability converting across IANA timezones.
Apply provider availability templates and buffer times.
Maintain distributed cache of public availability.

architecture_components.name: Booking and Transaction Manager
responsibilities: Process booking reservations with atomic database row-level locking.
Enforce cancellation policy rules and cutoff deadlines.
Emit booking state transitions to notification services.

data_entities.name: UserAccount
data_entities.purpose: Stores user profile data, credentials, role designations (Customer, Provider, Admin), and default timezone.

data_entities.name: ProviderSchedule
data_entities.purpose: Defines provider recurring availability, blackout dates, timezone identifier, and cancellation policy rules.

data_entities.name: Appointment
data_entities.purpose: Represents a booked service instance, containing start and end UTC timestamps, status, customer ID, provider ID, and lock versions.

data_entities.name: CancellationPolicy
data_entities.purpose: Defines the notice window hours, refund percentage, and penalty rules for appointment cancellations.

api_operations.purpose: Retrieve open booking slots for a provider projected into the requester's desired timezone.
Create a new appointment reservation using transactional concurrency control.
api_operations.authorization: Customer role with active account status

api_operations.purpose: Configure working hours, timezones, and cancellation policy settings.
Cancel a previously booked appointment subject to policy constraints.
api_operations.authorization: Customer owning the appointment or Provider assigned to the appointment

tests.description: Simulate 100 simultaneous booking requests on the exact same provider slot to verify that only one booking succeeds and 99 receive conflict errors without double-booking.
Verify that a user with a Customer role cannot invoke provider schedule update endpoints or access another customer's appointment details.
Validate timezone conversions across daylight saving time shifts for availability generation and appointment creation between UTC, America/New_York, and Asia/Tokyo.
Verify that an appointment cancellation requested past the cancellation policy cutoff window is rejected, while a cancellation before the cutoff succeeds and frees up the slot.

obligation_coverage.design_response: Implemented transactional isolation with pessimistic row-level locking and unique composite database constraints on provider_id and appointment time range within the Booking Manager component.
Configured JWT-based role-based access control in the Identity and Access Management service with explicit claim checks restricting customer and provider endpoints.
Standardized all internal timestamp representations to UTC ISO-8601 while maintaining IANA timezone identifiers on schedules and customer requests to dynamically project slots.

Created configurable cancellation policy entities and business logic in the Booking Manager that evaluate cancellation lead time against appointment start time before authorizing cancellations and releases.
Designed automated multi-threaded load test simulating race conditions on identical time slots to ensure transactional atomicity and conflict response codes.

assumptions.statement: Providers operate in a single primary timezone per location rather than dynamic multi-timezone mobile operations.
Late cancellations past the policy cutoff do not issue automatic payment refunds without manual provider intervention.
Appointments are booked in discrete fixed-duration increments rather than arbitrary custom duration blocks.
